localChanges: Computer players' units with nowhere in particular to go no longer drift north: they pick fairly among equally good squares, and carry straight on where they can (closes #284).
A computer player's unit whose move goes nowhere now stops for the turn, instead of trying the same move over and over (closes #446).

log: For civ-clone/web-renderer#284: the greedy step broke ties with a random comparator, which isn't a fair shuffle. With eight tied neighbours the first listed (North) was taken about 53% of the time. The scored steps are now shuffled with the game's RNG (Fisher–Yates, `lib/shuffle`) and sorted by score alone (stable). Among tied steps, the one straight on from the unit's last step comes first, which keeps a wandering unit heading somewhere: with a plain fair pick the arena read power −2.0, powerUnits −2.4 and shields −2.0 (t) on seeds 1–40 (flat on 41–80); with the heading no metric reaches |t| ≥ 2 on either set.

For civ-clone/web-renderer#446: `moveUnit` now stands a unit down (`noOrders`) when the action it takes, on its path or as the greedy step, leaves its tile, its moves and its active state as they were, instead of choosing the same step until the loop check gives up after 1,000 rounds.
